claim: On CAMI marine sample0, minco low-abundance readwise ANI misses are mainly an effective-coverage and shared-coverage assignment problem rather than only a raw distance-model problem; oracle effective-coverage AAF improved species F1 from 0.731 to 0.841.
caveat: Single CAMI sample; oracle uses Sylph Eff_cov and is not deployable without a minco-native effective-coverage estimator.

claim: On CAMI marine sample0, best-diff-unique readwise assignment plus ZIP-corrected context AAF ANI improved minco S10000 species F1 to 0.860 by direct CLI, exceeding local Sylph F1 0.831 on the same gold/taxmap scoring path.
caveat: Single CAMI sample and local OPAL-like scoring; needs more CAMI samples and official OPAL validation.

claim: On CAMI II marine short-read samples 0-2, minco S10000 best-diff-unique plus ZIP AAF beat local Sylph mean species F1, 0.860 versus 0.832, mainly by reducing mean FP from 60.7 to 41.3 at nearly equal recall.
caveat: Local OPAL-like taxid scoring only; minco and Sylph use different GTDB releases, and official OPAL validation plus samples 3-9 are still needed.

claim: On CAMI II marine short-read samples 0-2, minco S1000 GTDB-only matched S10000 accuracy and was much more efficient: mean F1 0.862 versus 0.860, mean runtime 124.5s versus 169.8s, and peak RSS 3.70GB versus 33.65GB.
caveat: Marine replicate samples only; needs a different dataset and official OPAL-style validation before setting S1000 as a general default.

claim: On CAMI3 Toy Human Gut sample0 and CAMI2 Marine sample0, a simple unique-primary/split-rescue hybrid threshold rule did not generalize: split mode improved recall, but the joint hybrid rule did not beat local Sylph or the best unique baseline.
caveat: Only two samples and local species-taxid scoring; same-sample tuned hybrid thresholds can improve individual datasets but are not valid defaults.

claim: On CAMI II marine samples 0-2 plus CAMI III Toy Human Gut samples 0-2, a random-forest minco call model using joined unique/split readwise features improved local species-level mean F1 to 0.745 versus 0.725 for local Sylph and 0.646 for the fixed minco direct threshold.
caveat: Local species-taxid scoring only; toy scoring is bacteria-only; minco and Sylph use different GTDB releases; needs a third distinct domain and official OPAL-style validation before release.

claim: On a nine-sample CAMI panel spanning marine0-2, Toy Human Gut0-2, and plant-associated0-2, a no-dataset-label minco RF/HGB averaged call model with strict/relaxed rule-evidence features improved local species-level mean F1 to 0.698 versus 0.676 for local Sylph and 0.598 for fixed minco unique direct.
caveat: Local species-taxid scoring only; toy and plant scoring are bacteria-only; minco and Sylph use different GTDB releases; still needs independent datasets, official OPAL validation, and production-model distillation.

claim: On external CAMI II strain-madness short-read samples 0-2, the current train9 RF/HGB averaged minco call model failed to beat local Sylph: mean F1 0.466 versus 0.527 for Sylph, while minco candidates still contained 17 of 20 gold species per sample.
caveat: Local species-taxid scoring only; minco and Sylph use different GTDB releases; three gold species were absent from current GTDB/taxmap mapping; result argues against exporting the current ensemble as a default.

claim: On CAMI II Toy Mouse Gut sample0, sample-specific source-aware scoring using CAMISIM source genomes showed that GTDB representative taxonomy caused most of the apparent exact-taxid failure: Sylph improved from F1 0.758 to 0.968 and minco train9 RF/HGB improved from 0.738 to 0.921.
caveat: Local source-aware scoring is valid for CAMISIM benchmarks but uses sample source genomes unavailable in real deployment; minco still did not beat Sylph on mouse sample0 after correction.

claim: On CAMI II Toy Mouse Gut sample0, GTDB S2000 context-markerdb after AAF 0.03 dedup improved minco unique direct GTDB-species F1 from 0.862 to 0.878; adding naive ANI with a high-depth breadth floor reached F1 0.892 with the Poisson-depth context filter.
caveat: Single CAMISIM sample; dedup removed only 182 of 200709 refs; GTDB truth uses unique GCF/GCA assembly-core fallback for 12 of 75 source genomes; breadth-depth cutoffs are empirically chosen here and need replication; Ref_zip_af>=0.5 was too conservative.

claim: On CAMI II Toy Mouse Gut samples 0-2, adding a Sylph-like robust effective-depth abundance estimator to MinCO ctx-markerdb reduced GTDB-species mean L1 error from 17.0 to 2.53 percentage points, but robust depth alone still did not beat Sylph at 2.29.
caveat: Three-sample Toy Mouse benchmark only; constants median>=20 and AF exponent 1.05 are empirical; superseded for final abundance L1 by C012 after adding an intra-genus winner rescue.

claim: On CAMI II Toy Mouse Gut samples 0-2, MinCO ctx-marker robust effective depth plus a conservative intra-genus winner rescue beat Sylph on GTDB-species abundance L1: 1.79 versus 2.29 percentage points.
caveat: Three-sample Toy Mouse benchmark only; the rescue uses GTDB genus/species mapping and empirical thresholds; Sylph still has better presence recall and rank correlation, so this is an abundance-L1 result, not a complete profiler win.

claim: On CAMI3 Toy Human Gut samples 0-2, the Toy Mouse intra-genus winner rescue did not transfer: it rescued zero species, while robust MinCO ctx+obj abundance improved L1 from 46.61 to 32.63 percentage points but remained worse than Sylph at 27.79.
caveat: CAMI bacterial NCBI species-taxid scoring, not GTDB species scoring; strict rescue rule was transferred unchanged; a CAMI3-specific calibration may behave differently.

claim: On the six-sample mouse GTDB plus CAMI3 NCBI mixed abundance panel, row-level leave-one-sample-out MinCO abundance calibration did not improve over raw value_sum and did not beat Sylph: best raw MinCO L1 was 17.82 versus Sylph 15.04.
caveat: Only six samples; model selection was on the same panel; mouse and CAMI3 use different truth namespaces; result points toward read-level or EM-style mass assignment rather than row-level regression.

claim: On the six-sample mouse GTDB plus CAMI3 NCBI benchmark, the full S2000 marked-unique proxy slightly improved old MinCO ctx-marker but did not beat Sylph or the current mixed MinCO rows for F1/abundance; MinCO coden15 still slightly beat Sylph adjusted ANI on the CAMI3 source/ref ANI subset.
caveat: Proxy result is now confirmed and superseded by integrated implementation claim C016; F1/abundance use mixed truth namespaces and only six samples.

claim: The integrated `minco ani --readwise-dual-evidence` full S2000 implementation reproduced the previous marked-unique proxy on the six-sample mouse GTDB plus CAMI3 NCBI benchmark, and aggregate full-S2000 add-back/EM proxies still did not beat Sylph or the current mixed MinCO rows for F1/abundance.
caveat: Only six samples; marker/full fallback thresholds were inherited from the proxy experiment and not retuned; aggregate EM used per-reference totals rather than true context/read ambiguity groups, so it tests only a proxy for shared-context assignment.

claim: On CAMI II Toy Mouse Gut, true read/context-level ambiguity edge dumps worked, but fixed edge-EM abundance blending is not a default candidate: raw EM worsened sample0 L1, and the best mouse0-2 fixed-beta mean was beta 0 (marker L1 3.0361 pp versus best positive beta 3.0368 pp).
caveat: Edge groups with more than 64 candidates were skipped; EM was restricted to marker-supported species and ambiguous groups only; sample0 and sample2 can improve with sample-specific beta, so this rejects fixed global blending, not all possible adaptive context-level EM designs.

claim: The guarded `universal-auto-exact` MinCO calibrated profile wrapper is the current F1-priority default: on the 26-sample mixed panel it improves mean F1 over the legacy probability gate (0.7093 versus 0.6962), and on CAMI III Toy Human Gut samples 0-5 it beats Sylph mean F1 (0.7647 versus 0.6849) while reducing FP+FN.
caveat: Local taxid/GTDB-transfer scoring only; Sylph still has better CAMI III abundance L1/Pearson, and final cross-dataset claims need systematic GTDB truth transfer plus more unseen benchmark types.

claim: As of 2026-06-27, the best supported single MinCO default is `universal-auto-exact` with guarded exact split, high-extra low-uAF probability-tail rescue, and low-extra split rescue; this is a best-known MinCO F1-priority default, not a proven universal Sylph-beating strategy.
caveat: CAMI II Toy Mouse samples5-7, HMP gastrooral, and HMP airskin source-abundance still favor Sylph for F1 and abundance L1/Pearson; CAMI III partial source-readmap transfer supports MinCO F1 but maps only 81.2684% mean read-row mass and Sylph remains better for abundance; release-readiness audit is pre_release_candidate because only 1/5 panels are clean release-grade GTDB truth, and C minco profile is documented as a conservative direct/domain path rather than the calibrated species default.

claim: For calibrated MinCO profile output, ZIP-AAF ANI should be exposed as `reported_ani`: it is closer to source/ref ANI than raw emitted MinCO ANI on Toy Mouse and is close to Sylph Adjusted_ANI on CAMI3 source/ref, but it is diagnostic rather than a universal Sylph-beating ANI claim.
caveat: Toy Mouse source-to-representative ANIm still favors Sylph Adjusted_ANI; `reported_ani` is a reporting field and does not change call or abundance logic.

claim: As of 2026-06-30, the achievable MinCO release goal is supported: `scripts/minco_profile` provides a single default command, `--check-ref` validates packaged references, sidecar defaults avoid expert domain flags, and the current candidate preset is supported versus previous MinCO defaults with explicit claim boundaries.
caveat: This is a release-readiness/user-usability claim, not a universal Sylph-beating or abundance-superiority claim; the broad research objective remains incomplete until release-grade holdout and abundance gaps close.
